issues.problem: The Evaluate stage relies only on open-ended reflection questions and gives no embedded demo-based or oral exit-ticket check, even though provenance marks 'assessment' missing for L1-s6 and T02 prescribes a two-person demo check or 2-minute oral exit ticket for this lesson.
issues.fix: Insert a lightweight two-person demo check (one shakes, partner predicts the three outcomes and states the choice logic) or an oral exit-ticket into the Evaluate slide so understanding is observable.

issues.problem: The session offers only an open-ended Extend with no paired support tier for struggling learners, while provenance lists 'differentiation' missing and T01 prescribes paired support-and-stretch for the rock-paper-scissors lesson.
issues.fix: Add an explicit support option such as a pre-built remix project or a single-branch if/then skeleton alongside the existing stretch challenge so all learners reach the shake-and-random core.

issues.problem: The deck carries no worked-solution success criteria for the RPS program; T03 notes the upstream RPS answer-key was dropped and provenance lists 'answer_key' missing, yet slide 5 only narrates logic instead of defining canonical correct/incorrect checks.
issues.fix: Author a short answer key stating the canonical shake to random 1-3 to show rock/paper/scissors mapping plus common mistakes to flag (fixed outcome, missing shake handler, incomplete three-way mapping).

issues.problem: Slide 5 labels the selection a single 'if then else' block, but the canonical program is an if/else-if/else chain performing a three-way mapping, and the digest itself later describes nested ifs, so the simplification can misrepresent block structure to beginners.
issues.fix: Describe the selection as an if/else-if/else chain so the stated block structure matches the canonical three-outcome logic.

issues.problem: Slide 5 'examine the code' bundles four distinct concepts (gesture trigger, random variable, conditional logic, three-way icon mapping) onto one slide, conflicting with T05/Merrill and Sweller one-idea-per-slide and chunking guidance for young learners.
issues.fix: Split the code examination into separate mini-steps (trigger, variable, condition, icons), one concept per slide, before the build.

issues.problem: Slide 12 asserts the micro:bit is 'more fair than a human because it can't cheat,' yet pick random is a pseudo-random deterministic PRNG and the deck's own slide 3 invites the 'truly random' question, so the Share note overstates fairness without noting pseudo-randomness.
issues.fix: Reframe the fairness note to acknowledge the generator is pseudo-random and the fairness advantage is about not cheating rather than true randomness.
